newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian airline seeks Balkan alliance.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian airline seeks Balkan alliance.

text.p: Bulgaria's state carrier Balkan Airlines hopes to set up a regional alliance of Balkan airlines on the model of Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS), a spokesman said on Monday.
Balkan spokesman Viktor Melamed said the company had not yet started talks with neighbouring countries on uniting their airlines but "the idea has been presented to some ministers".

"We cannot survive as individual companies under today's conditions among such mastodons as British Airways or Lufthansa, and our idea is to unite in a stock company like SAS by the year 2000," Melamed told Reuters.
SAS is owned jointly by the governments of Denmark, Sweden and Norway and private investors.
Melamed said Balkan would invite for talks the national carriers of Romania, Macedonia, Yugoslavia, Croatia and Greece but any decision would have to be taken at government level.
He said the companies would share planes and routes, with profits and costs distributed according to the size of the member's stake.
Balkan plans to renovate its international passenger fleet, which consists mainly of Soviet-made aircraft, before the firm is offered for privatisation next year.
Balkan said Airbus Industrie officials had made their proposals last week in Sofia.

Boeing representatives are due to present their offer next week and Russia's Tupolev is expected at the end of the month, Melamed said, adding that Tupolev aircraft could be purchased only for charter flights as the company did not have a range of different-sized planes. -- Liliana Semerdjieva, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-91188
